messages.subject: DoubleArrayVector and DoubleVector
messages.body_plain:
I'm trying to have an existing class in my software extend DoubleVector in the same way that DoubleArrayVector does.  Basically I have a class that I want to act like a DoubleVector, but it uses a different data storage protocol than DoubleArrayVector.

But, the abstract class DoubleVector uses DoubleArrayVector (which itself extends DoubleVector).  For example, newCopyBuilder in DoubleVector returns a DoubleArrayVector.Builder.

This makes it, as far as I can tell, impossible to simply extend DoubleVector which seems to defeat the purpose of having it as an abstract class in the first place.

Is it necessary to use this design, rather than, for example, having newCopyBuilder (and similar methods) return a DoubleVector.Builder?

Thanks,

Bruce

messages.subject: Apache Commons Math version
messages.body_plain:
Renjin currently uses Apache Commons Math version 2.2, rather than a newer 3.x version.

Is there a plan to switch to 3.6  (or alternatively to the commons math fork at hipparchus.org <http://hipparchus.org> ).

It would be nice to take advantage of some newer features in 3.x, and I have a problem because my code uses Complex objects from Commons Math 3.x, so I have to convert Complex objects used in renjin from the 2.x versions.

Thanks,

Bruce

messages.subject: Re: DoubleArrayVector and DoubleVector
messages.body_plain:
Hi Bruce,

That's exactly right. The bare minimum for implementing your own DoubleVector are:
1. getElementAsDouble()
2. length()
3. cloneWithNewAttributes()

The simplest example is probably DoubleSequence <https://github.com/bedatadriven/renjin/blob/6089bb33fd70e56e4f15bfbf645814c25b968ca8/core/src/main/java/org/renjin/primitives/sequence/DoubleSequence.java#L32-L32>, which doesn't store anything beyond the start and end of the sequence.

But you're right about the builder API -- DoubleVector.newCopyBuilder should return DoubleVector.Builder and not DoubleArrayVector.Builder. I think this should be possible to correct without breaking anything.

Best,
Alex

messages.body_plain:
I am doing a survey of what R packages are available for renjin. This is in support of a project to develop Processing.R, a renjin-based R mode for the Processing language/IDE.

Is there a way to find a listing from packages.renjin.org <http://packages.renjin.org> of anything that "passed all tests"?

I have only found the search interface, and with so many packages from BioConductor and CRAN it has been very slow going trying to get a sense of what is available -- out of the first ten that I tried scattershot (graph, lubridate, pcaMethods, stringr, etc.),  I only found one with an affirmative listing (plyr).

messages.subject: Re: List from packages.renjin that have passed all tests?
messages.subject_clean: List from packages.renjin that have passed all tests?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jeremy,

I love Processing, therefore this sounds incredibly interesting. I have always felt that Renjin is a great match for Processing and I have put together a little example <https://gist.github.com/mjkallen/8299891> in the past to demonstrate how easy it is to load Renjin into a Processing sketch. I'd love to learn more about your ideas regarding this "R mode" for Processing, do you have any public project/information available to share?

We can query our build system to get you the information you are looking for. But be aware: passing all tests currently only means that none of the examples in a package result in an error. There are packages with little or no examples, or even just very trivial examples, therefore this is not a 100% guarantee that the package will work flawlessly in Renjin.

Regards,

Maarten-Jan Kallen

messages.subject: Re: List from packages.renjin that have passed all tests?
messages.subject_clean: List from packages.renjin that have passed all tests?
messages.body_plain:
Thank you so much, Maarten-Jan --

Please do query the build system for passing packages -- I would greatly appreciate it. I understand that test passing isn't a guarantee, but it would be a great first-pass to help begin a search.

Very glad to hear that you find the project interesting -- and thanks for sharing that example!

Processing.R is a Google Summer of Code 2017 project proposed by the very talented Ce Gao -- I am acting as his GSOC mentor on behalf of the Processing Foundation. Just as the "Processing.py" Python Mode uses Jython to enable Processing-in-Python, the "Processing.R" R Language Mode uses Renjin to enable coding Processing-in-R. Part of the early work is in mapping out calls to the Processing(Java) API -- e.g. `processing$line(x,y,x2,y2)` -- and later in using pre-processing to make the API automagically available as a top-level namespace.

There is a working alpha-level R Language mode for the command line and the Processing Development Environment (PDE) available here:

https://github.com/gaocegege/Processing.R

At present the release is old, and the latest mode should instead be built and installed with ant from master. Sometime soon we should have the mode integrated with PDE's built-in Contributions Manager for casual testing. If you or other members of the Renjin community are interested then we will keep you in the loop -- feedback and ideas would be most welcome.

very best,
Jeremy

messages.subject: Re: [Ask for advice] Support float in Renjin
messages.subject_clean: [Ask for advice] Support float in Renjin
messages.body_plain:
Hi Ce Gao,
Indeed, Renjin was not correctly handling arguments of type float or float[]. I've opened an issue here:
https://github.com/bedatadriven/renjin/issues/319

And comitted a quick fix. A new release should be available shortly.

Best,
ALex

On Mon, May 29, 2017 at 3:49 AM Ce Gao <gaoc...@gmail.com> wrote:

> Hi, all
>
> Recently I have a project: Processing.R <https://github.com/gaocegege/Processing.R>, which is the mode in Processing to allow users to write Processing sketches in R. Processing is written in Java, and the functions' parameters are all float:
>
> /*
>  * Draws a line (a direct path between two points) to the screen.
>  * @param x1 x-coordinate of the first point
>  * @param y1 y-coordinate of the first point
>  * @param x2 x-coordinate of the second point
>  * @param y2 y-coordinate of the second point
>  */
> public void line(float x1, float y1, float x2, float y2) {
>   // Draw a line in the canvas.
> }
>
> There is only double(DoubleVector) in Renjin, no float. To add those functions into R, I have to:
>
> public void line(double x1, double y1, double x2, double y2) {
>   super.line((float) posAX, (float) posAY, (float) posBX, (float) posBY);
> }
>
> Is there some suggestions to add float type in Renjin, or other graceful ways to avoid manual cast?
>
> Thanks for your time.
>
